identity.title: Make governance signals scope-aware without changing rule meaning

human_pressure.one_screen_brief: Ensure governance signals are attributed to the correct execution scope so validation, backend, review, approval, budget, authority, and inconsistency signals do not accidentally mix independent scopes inside one run.
human_pressure.why_now: Once scope exists on canonical facts and records, signal attribution must preserve the same governance subject boundary.
do_not_misread: Do not change severity unless an existing rule is demonstrably wrong and separately evidenced.
Do not infer scope from signal text or subject.
red_lines: No outcome changes in this pack.

machine_core.goal: Add optional scope attribution to GovernanceSignal generation and apply it consistently where the triggering evidence already has an explicit scope_ref.
red_lines: Do not alter existing rule predicates except where needed to prevent cross-scope contamination.
Do not invent scope for run-level facts.
Do not change signal severity taxonomy.
Do not introduce a new BLOCKED or HUMAN_REVIEW path.
invariants: A signal belongs to the scope of its triggering evidence when explicitly known.
Signal IDs remain deterministic and must include scope if scope changes signal identity.

observable_effect.assertion: Signals preserve governance-subject attribution and independent scopes do not create cross-scope signal contamination.

proofs.assertion: Signal tests prove scope attribution, deterministic IDs, and unscoped compatibility.

failure_semantics: Signals with different scope identity must not collapse to the same deterministic signal identity when all other evidence is equal.

steps.title: Add scope attribution to signal identity
details: Carry optional scope_ref on GovernanceSignal or equivalent canonical signal representation.

steps.title: Apply scope to record-backed signals
details: Authority, approval, and budget signals inherit explicit record scope.

steps.title: Protect run-level rules
details: Keep genuinely run-level signals unscoped and avoid manufacturing scope.

steps.title: Prove compatibility
details: Cover scoped, unscoped, replay-deterministic, and independent-scope cases.

acceptance: Signals can expose scope_ref when evidence supports it.
Independent scopes do not collapse signal identity.
No new signal family or severity change is introduced.
validate: python -m pytest tests/test_governance_signals.py tests/test_authority_governance.py tests/test_approval_governance.py tests/test_budget_governance.py -q

must_check: Scope comes from triggering evidence/records, not inference.
Run-level signals are not forcibly scoped.
reject_if: Signal scope is inferred from text, subject, ordering, or producer names.

validation_notes.targeted_contract_coverage: Existing signal and governance-record suites directly cover scope attribution while full suite protects replay and reporting compatibility.
